text:
fiona: quick follow-up from the iterator workshop: we need a clear contract for resume tokens vs idempotency tokens for paginated endpoints. main pain: clients want retry+resume but pages aren't always idempotent (server-side ordering/side-effects). thoughts?

greg: short answer: separate concerns. resume tokens = read-only scan position. idempotency tokens = write dedupe. mixing them leads to surprising resumptions.

hannah: agree. concrete: mark endpoints as READ-PAGINABLE vs SIDE-EFFECT-PAGINABLE in the spec. only READ-PAGINABLE endpoints get strong resume guarantees.

fiona: good. for READ-PAGINABLE we should guarantee token monotonicity and short-lived stability window (server TTL). for SIDE-EFFECT-PAGINABLE we return a warning header and no resume promise.

ian: SDK surface implications: two iterator types: ReadIterator (supports resume, cursor object, expiry metadata) and TaskIterator (no resume, throws if you try to resume). keeps ergonomics explicit.

julia: ergonomics nit: many users will want a simple for-await-of / for loop. can we make the read iterator implement the same shape across languages?

greg: we can. proposal:
- TS: AsyncIterable for ReadIterator (browser + node). include .cursor property with expiresAt and refresh() method. default: no auto-refresh in browser.
- Python: generator + AsyncIterator; Cursor helper with .refresh() and contextmanager to auto-refresh if user sets auto_refresh=True.
- Go: provide PageIterator.Next(ctx) returns (items, cursor, err). Cursor is small struct with ExpiresAt and Refresh(ctx) method.

hannah: retry behaviour: reads should be idempotent, so we can safely retry pages. For streaming endpoints we need to be careful (partial page returned). recommend server side always return complete page or error; partial pages only allowed with explicit chunked API.

fiona: what about back-compat and small clients that only store the cursor string? We should keep the cursor string forward-compatible: encoded format v1:{base64payload}. the SDKs can parse and expose fields, but raw strings still work.

ian: cancellation semantics: Go/py users expect context/cancel to abort underlying request but keep iterator usable. if cancellation occurs mid-page, iterator should surface ErrCancelled and leave cursor unchanged so user can resume later.
julia: logging/telemetry: emit pagination_event with action=[issue|resume|expire|fail] and labels endpoint, env, user_tier. Keep payload small.
greg: server hints: besides recommended_retry_window, include `X-Page-Complete: 1/0` and `X-Cursor-Version: v1` headers. useful for proxies and SDKs.
hannah: tests: fuzz cursor decoding, simulate partial network failures, simulate leader failover that forces early invalidation -> server returns CursorInvalidated + suggested_restart_cursor if available. SDKs should translate to exception type CursorInvalidated with metadata.
fiona: docs: clearly document that resume is a hint not a guarantee on Dedicated if admin toggles long-running GC. we'll expose env-specific defaults via /v1/meta or headers.
greg: one more SDK API request: expose a small helper function `RetryWithinWindow(policy, windowSec)` that composes backoff until either attempts exhausted or window elapsed. This avoids every client re-implementing window logic.
julia: small UX: for TS, provide an option `{dedupeOnRestart: true}` that will attach a per-session idempotency token to requests to assist server-side dedupe. default false.

fiona: OK action items: 1) update pagination RFC with READ-PAGINABLE vs SIDE-EFFECT-PAGINABLE and header hints 2) implement Cursor struct/helper in py/ts/go with matching metadata fields 3) add RetryWithinWindow helper to SDK runtime 4) add interop tests & telemetry plan. Who picks which?
greg: i'll take RetryWithinWindow + TS iterator impl.
hannah: i'll own server header hints and CursorInvalidated shape.
ian: i'll do Go Cursor + tests.
julia: i'll add README snippets and telemetry labels.
